cim: SENATOR PAYANO: Artificial Intelligence Is Moving Fast, Our Laws Need to Keep Up
cim_eredeti: SENATOR PAYANO: Artificial Intelligence Is Moving Fast, Our Laws Need to Keep Up
szoveg_eredeti:
Artificial intelligence is no longer a technology of the future. It is already changing how we work, how students learn, how businesses operate and how information is created. That brings enormous opportunity, but it also raises questions government cannot afford to ignore.

Massachusetts has long been a leader in technology, research and innovation. We should want to remain at the forefront of AI. But leadership cannot simply mean developing the newest technology. It also means establishing reasonable protections for the people who will be affected by it.

As Vice Chair of the Joint Committee on Advanced Information Technology, the Internet and Cybersecurity, this is a conversation I believe the Legislature will be having for years to come.

We have already started. In 2024, Massachusetts passed the FutureTech Act, authorizing $25 million for artificial intelligence and machine-learning projects that could improve state services. The Legislature also passed the Mass Leads Act, which included $103 million to support the development and application of Al in areas including health care, advanced manufacturing, robotics and education.

There is good reason to make those investments. AI has the potential to help researchers make discoveries faster, help small businesses become more productive and improve the way government delivers services.

But investment must also come with accountability. We need to examine what happens when AI helps determine whether someone receives medical treatment, gets considered for a job or qualifies for housing. We need to protect people’s personal information.

We need to address increasingly realistic deepfakes and deceptive AI-generated content. And as AI changes the workplace, workers need to be part of that conversation. There is also a question of transparency. If an automated system plays a significant role in a decision that affects your life, you should have some understanding of how that decision was made and who is ultimately accountable for it.

At the same time, we have to be thoughtful about how we regulate. There is an important difference between a small business using Al to become more efficient and one of the world’s largest technology companies developing an extraordinarily powerful AI model. Our laws should recognize that difference.

We also cannot expect one piece of legislation to solve every problem associated with artificial intelligence. The technology is changing too quickly.

That means lawmakers need to continue listening to researchers, workers, educators, businesses, consumer advocates and the people developing these systems. As the technology evolves, our understanding of the risks and our laws will have to evolve with it.

Massachusetts does not have to choose between innovation and protecting people. We can support the researchers, entrepreneurs and businesses building the next generation of technology while establishing reasonable expectations for transparency, accountability and safety.

That work has started. It is far from finished.

Pavel Payano is a Democrat Massachusetts State Senator representing Haverhill, Methuen, and Lawrence. He is also a former Lawrence City Councilor and School Committeeman. To reach his office you can e-mail: Sharoline.Galva@masenate.gov ◊
